# Bibliographic Requirements Checklist: Academic Catalog Workflow

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, and measurability of the revised bibliographic model, format mappings, and preservation requirements before task generation.
**Created**: 2026-09-20
**Feature**: [Academic Catalog Workflow](../spec.md)
**Focus and Depth**: Standard-depth review, emphasizing semantic coverage and migration/export fidelity.
**Actor and Timing**: Project author/reviewer, after the targeted standards revision and before `$speckit-tasks`.

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by `$speckit-checklist` from the current feature and the preceding standards discussion. Its focus is inferred from that discussion; no additional scope or product decisions are implied.
**Review Ownership**: This is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines that the written requirements satisfy the criterion.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` records satisfaction of a requirements-quality criterion, not implementation completion or passing interoperability tests. All generated items are unchecked.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the bibliographic baseline, additional citation vocabularies, and boundaries of refs-owned metadata explicitly identified without implying universal format compatibility? [Completeness, Spec §Bibliographic semantic scope; Spec §FR-047]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. Zotero v45, CSL and BibLaTeX 3.22 pins are identified with hashes and non-universality disclaimers (Bibliography §Normative vocabulary inventory; hashes re-verified). But the `bibtex` namespace and `refs-bibtex-v1` profile have no vocabulary at all, and legacy fields/type aliases defined outside `blx-dm.def` (`year`, `month`, `journal`, `address`, `school`, `phdthesis`, `techreport`) are unidentified although they are 100% of the user's manuscript bibliographies. The baseline is also 17 schema versions ahead of the installed Zotero 6.0.37 (global schema 28). [F-B03, F-I06, F-S01]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the documented coverage account for every baseline type, field, and contributor role with an explicit structured path or a justified limitation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-047; Bibliography §Normative vocabulary inventory; Coverage registry]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. All 40 types and 770 type-field rows match the pinned schema exactly (structured comparison), but the 37 Zotero creator types carry only `creatorType`/`primary` with no canonical role or equivalence (castMember/performer, podcaster/host, bookAuthor/container-author, seriesEditor/collection-editor). The 51 BibLaTeX entry types have no shared-type projection, and every row's limitation/export text is one identical string, so no limitation is 'justified'. [F-B02, F-B04, F-B05]
- [x] CHK003 Are creation, inspection, correction, and full-export requirements specified for recognized native fields as well as common bibliographic fields? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-042, §FR-047]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied as a statement of requirements: FR-047, Records §Source Creation/§Patch Semantics, CLI `show`, and Interchange §Full Library Export each name native fields. Caveat: which path an author should use for a given fact is undermined by duplicate authorities, assessed under CHK009. [F-B01]
- [ ] CHK004 Are notes, attachments, annotations, and asserted source relationships each given explicit identity, content, parent/target, and usability requirements? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023, §FR-049; Bibliography §Supporting items and asserted relationships]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. Identity, kind and parent are defined (Data model `supporting_items`, `source_relations`), but content is not: where note HTML and annotation text/comment/colour/position/page label live (row, `metadata JSON`, or only the snapshot BLOB) is unstated; an attachment's own note (246 in the user's library), standalone attachments in collections (3), snapshots as a distinct kind, trash, `dc:replaces` and `owl:sameAs` are absent; uniqueness is 'within kind' while Zotero keys are per library. Usability is only 'read-only inspection', with no removal rule. [F-B07, F-I06]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK005 Are ingestion, structured usability, indexing, target-specific export, and original preservation defined as separate guarantees with clear meanings? [Clarity, Spec §FR-048; Bibliography §Independent coverage guarantees]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied. Bibliography §Independent coverage guarantees defines five dimensions with distinct obligations and FR-048 requires them to be reported separately. The residual vagueness of 'supported' inside the Usable row is assessed under CHK033. [F-Q03]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the boundary between recognized editable native metadata, custom fields, and immutable original expressions unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-005, §FR-047; Bibliography §One authoritative value per fact]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. Four buckets exist (`citation_fields`, `extensions.<ns>.fields`, top-level `extra`, immutable `native_fields`) but: BibLaTeX `usera-f`/`lista-f`/`verba-c` and Zotero `extra` are classed as recognized structured native fields though semantically custom; no rule says when export re-emits preserved TeX versus the canonical value ('Changing a mapped semantic field invalidates its stale lexical output representation' implies two emission paths); Zotero `extra` is simultaneously one native field and a container of separately parsed directives and the `Citation Key:` line. [F-B01, F-I09]
- [ ] CHK007 Are the criteria for an essential citation error versus a permissible reported omission defined precisely enough to avoid reviewer-dependent output decisions? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-048; Bibliography §Named output profiles]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. 'Essential citation semantics', 'essential unresolved fact' and 'when citation authorship would change' have no decision rule in Spec FR-039/FR-048 or Bibliography §Named output profiles; two reviewers would decide differently. Applied literally with the v1 type table it blocks 8 of 9 surveyed real bibliographies. [F-I02, F-I01]
- [ ] CHK008 Are the evidence and recorded decision needed for a “reviewed fallback,” “verified flattening,” or ambiguous subtype reconciliation specified? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Bibliography §Named output profiles; Bibliography §Inheritance, macros, and Better BibTeX Extra]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. 'Reviewed fallback', 'explicit review recorded for that source', 'verified flattening' and 'reconciled' subtype have no evidence requirement, no actor, and no field or table in the data model or records contract to hold the recorded decision. [F-I02]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Do the specification, records contract, and mapping inventory consistently assign one authoritative editable value to shared facts and format aliases? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, §FR-047; Records §Bibliographic profile; Coverage registry]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied; this is the central defect. Structured comparison of the registry with Zotero's own CSL crosswalk shows 51 of 121 Zotero fields assigned a Zotero-native path while the same fact also has a CSL/core path (e.g. `thesisType`/`reportType` vs `publication.genre` vs BibLaTeX `type`; `reportNumber`/`patentNumber` vs `publication.number`; Zotero `institution`/`university` -> `publication.publishers` but BibLaTeX `institution` -> `publication.institutions`; `scale`, `section`, `references`, `partTitle`, `chapter`, `eprint`/`archiveID`, `holder`/`assignee`). This contradicts Bibliography §One authoritative value per fact. [F-B01]
- [x] CHK010 Are accepted author/editor key fallback requirements clearly separated from target-specific citation-author projections for inventors, programmers, and presenters? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-007; Bibliography §Titles, people, dates, and publication structure]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied. Bibliography §Titles, people, dates (paragraph after the table), Data model `creators` row and Quickstart §Bibliographic profile acceptance all keep the literal author -> editor -> title key fallback separate from target author projection. Consequence to note: inventor-only and programmer-only records receive title-led keys. [no finding]
- [ ] CHK011 Are source title, title without subtitle, container title, and multivolume title meanings consistent across the requirements and each format mapping? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009, §FR-048; Bibliography §Titles, people, dates, and publication structure]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. The `main_title` vs BibLaTeX `maintitle` hazard is handled explicitly, but the three-level hierarchy has two encodings: core `multivolume_title`/`container_title` and CSL `citation_fields.volume-title`/`part-title`. Executed Pandoc 3.11 maps `maintitle` -> `container-title` (chapter) or `title` (book) and `booktitle`/`title` -> `volume-title`, which the contract's mapping does not state. [F-B01, F-I05]
- [x] CHK012 Are standalone supporting items consistently permitted without an invented source across import outcomes, entity relationships, inspection, and full export? [Consistency, Spec §FR-049; Data model §Entities and Relationships; Interchange §Full Library Export v1]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied. Nullable parent plus unresolved parent origin (Data model `supporting_items`, invariant 2), `import_entries` applied entity kind, CLI `import show`, and Interchange `supporting-items.jsonl` are mutually consistent about standalone items without an invented source. Removal of such items is unspecified (see CHK004). [F-B07]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK013 Does “zero unaccounted” vocabulary coverage define its denominator, applicable schema baseline, and acceptable limitation statuses? [Measurability, Spec §SC-010; Bibliography §Normative vocabulary inventory]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. SC-010 says 'documented baseline vocabulary' without stating whether the denominator is Zotero only or all three inventories, which statuses count as accounted (`structured-when-parsed`, `preservation-only`, `dependency-reference`), or the role rows. The registry is both the denominator and the mapping, so 'zero unaccounted' holds by construction and cannot fail. [F-B02, F-Q02]
- [x] CHK014 Do the acceptance requirements distinguish schema enumeration, structured-value preservation, and citation fidelity rather than allowing one to stand in for another? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, §SC-006, §SC-010]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied. SC-010, Bibliography §Normative vocabulary inventory ('necessary but does not demonstrate source-data preservation') and Research R3 keep enumeration, structured preservation and rendered citation distinct. Separate defect: the rendered-citation oracle is undefined and the internal CSL projection is not what the manuscript consumes. [F-I05, F-Q02]
- [x] CHK015 Are the representative sample's required types and difficult constructs specified, including when the nominal 30-record minimum must expand? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-002, §SC-010; Quickstart §Bibliographic profile acceptance]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied. SC-002 lists required types and edge-case classes; Quickstart §Bibliographic profile acceptance requires every type/construct used by the selected paper and expansion beyond 30 when needed. [no finding]
- [ ] CHK016 Are completeness criteria defined for each initially supported output mapping, including ordinary books and traditional BibTeX part records? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-006, §SC-010; Bibliography §Named output profiles, B01–B15]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. B14/B15 exist as rows but defer to 'the target report'; no mapping states which fields must appear in output for a record to count as complete, nor how literal editions are emitted. Several types present in the user's library (magazine/newspaper article, blog post, standard, presentation, manuscript, manual) have no row, and rows B04 and B05 emit fields that the contract's own validity rule rejects. [F-I01, F-I11, F-Q02]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements defined for structured agent submission, initial format ingestion, and later correction of the same recognized bibliographic facts? [Coverage, Primary/Alternate Flow, Spec §FR-001, §FR-018, §FR-021, §FR-047]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. Each route is individually required (FR-001, FR-018, FR-021, FR-047), but the routes do not converge on the same paths for the same fact, so 'later correction of the same recognized bibliographic facts' is not coherently specified; no requirement or fixture demands cross-route convergence. Agent submission also lacks a CSL-JSON or single-entry BibTeX input. [F-B01, F-Q02, F-S03]
- [ ] CHK018 Are unchanged reimport, conflicting incoming values, and correction of an inherited or native field covered without ambiguous precedence over human edits? [Coverage, Alternate/Exception Flow, Spec §FR-005, §FR-021, §FR-024; Records §Matching and Reconciliation]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. Unchanged reimport and conflicting values are covered (FR-021, Records §Matching and Reconciliation), but: whether a field absent from the incoming entry is a difference is undefined; a correction to an inherited (flattened) child value versus a later parent reimport has no precedence rule; bulk decisions are absent; BBT 8's relocation of keys from Extra to `citationKey` would flag every item as changed. [F-I07, F-I03, F-I06]
- [x] CHK019 Are unsupported selected sources and essential unresolved fields covered consistently by the bibliography publication and existing-output preservation requirements? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-038, §FR-039, §FR-048; Bibliography §Independent coverage guarantees]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied for consistency. FR-038/FR-039, Bibliography §Independent coverage guarantees ('blocks the entire bibliography publication') and Files §Bibliography Adoption and Export (no truncation, baseline not advanced) agree. The trigger itself is undefined (CHK007) and the policy is disproportionate. [F-I01, F-I02]
- [ ] CHK020 Are interruption, resumption, backup, and restoration requirements explicitly applicable to the newly added supporting records, native fields, and asserted relationships? [Coverage, Recovery Flow, Spec §FR-014, §FR-024, §FR-040–FR-042, §FR-049]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. Full export names supporting items and relations explicitly (Interchange), and backup covers them implicitly as one database, but FR-040-FR-042, SC-008 and the Quickstart restore comparison list omit them, and import resume semantics for supporting items rest on one table cell. Backup is also refused while any file operation is unresolved. [F-A07, F-B07]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK021 Are requirements explicit for native types that share one citation classification, and for preprints versus later published versions? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020, §FR-048; Bibliography §Named output profiles, B04/B13]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied. FR-020, the edge-case list, and B04/B13 state that shared CSL classification keeps native subtypes and that a preprint and its later article stay distinct absent reconciliation. [no finding]
- [ ] CHK022 Are traditional BibTeX and BibLaTeX part-record semantics distinguished, including how the input dialect is established when the file extension is ambiguous? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-018, §FR-048; Bibliography §Named output profiles, B02/B15]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. Dialect is a per-file `--format bibtex|biblatex` declaration (CLI), but every surveyed user file is `references.bib` with traditional fields and some BibLaTeX ones mixed in; no per-entry rule exists (e.g. presence of `booktitle` decides `@inbook` title meaning). Legacy type and field aliases are unspecified. [F-I04, F-B03]
- [ ] CHK023 Are corporate names, personal-name particles, suffixes, role namespaces, and conflicting name interpretations addressed without unspecified normalization? [Coverage, Spec §FR-002, §FR-008, §FR-048; Bibliography §Titles, people, dates, and publication structure]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. Particle/suffix fields and literal names are defined, but BibTeX has one `von` part and the contract refuses to infer ('Do not infer particle kinds'), so every particle name produces a diagnostic and may block export; Pandoc's actual rule (dropping unless `useprefix`) is not adopted or rejected. No role-equivalence table exists; `shortauthor`/`sortname` are modelled as creator roles; `editora` is separated from `editoratype`. [F-B04, F-B08]
- [ ] CHK024 Are incomplete/qualified dates, patent priority versus publication dates, descriptive editions, and inconsistent numeric interpretations given explicit preservation and conflict rules? [Coverage, Spec §FR-002, §FR-010, §FR-048; Bibliography §Titles, people, dates, and publication structure]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. Descriptive editions, numeric conflicts and patent priority date are covered, but `year`/`month` (the only date form in the user's files) and their conflict with `date` are absent; supported EDTF subset is 'the certified parser' with no parser named; season/circa exist without unspecified-digit or open-range forms. [F-B08, F-B03]
- [x] CHK025 Are missing/cyclic inheritance, child overrides, unselected parents, custom fields, and unresolved export directives each assigned a clear requirement outcome? [Coverage, Spec §FR-019, §FR-048; Bibliography §Inheritance, macros, and Better BibTeX Extra]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied as assigned outcomes: Bibliography §Inheritance, macros, and Better BibTeX Extra gives each case (missing/cyclic parent, child override, unselected parent, custom field, unresolved directive) a stated result. The inheritance subset itself contradicts BibLaTeX's `\DefaultInheritance{all=true}` and Pandoc's behaviour, and none of these constructs occurs in the user's corpus. [F-I03]
- [x] CHK026 Are URL-only attachments, missing parent links, standalone notes, and unresolved related-source targets covered without equating their preservation with openable-file usability? [Coverage, Spec §FR-023, §FR-026, §FR-049; Bibliography §Supporting items and asserted relationships]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied. Bibliography §Supporting items and asserted relationships separates record preservation from openable resources, covers URL-only and path-less attachments, standalone notes and unresolved targets, and requires real PDF checks for annotations. [no finding]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK027 Are imported rich text, expressions, and export directives explicitly treated as inert content, with clear boundaries on interpretation and disclosure? [Security/Ownership, Spec §FR-018, §FR-049; Bibliography §Supporting items and asserted relationships]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied. Raw TeX is never evaluated, `execute`/options are preservation-only, BBT directives are not applied silently, and rich text is not treated as trusted HTML (Bibliography §One authoritative value, §Inheritance, §Supporting items). Privacy of retained snapshot bytes is a separate gap. [F-A06]
- [x] CHK028 Are offline discovery and understandable structured diagnostics required for supported metadata paths and field-level mapping limitations? [Usability, Spec §FR-013, §FR-017, §FR-019, §FR-048]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied as a requirement: FR-013/FR-017, CLI `schema NAME`, and the per-source/field-path report in Bibliography §Independent coverage guarantees. Gaps noted elsewhere: no enumerated error-code registry, and Typer offers no machine introspection so `schema` must be refs-owned. [F-D03]
- [ ] CHK029 Do the stated scale and response-time requirements define whether large native metadata and supporting-record payloads fall within their scope? [Performance, Gap, Plan §Technical Context; CLI §Commands]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied (gap confirmed). Plan §Technical Context targets 10,000 sources/30,000 links for search/list only; nothing states whether `show` with supporting items, large notes, or a catalog carrying 75 MB snapshot BLOBs is in scope. Measured: twelve snapshots give an 897 MB catalog. [F-A06, F-Q04]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK030 Are upstream vocabulary versions, target profiles, and migration-layout assumptions separately documented with explicit upgrade consequences? [Dependency, Spec §FR-041, §FR-048; Bibliography §Normative vocabulary inventory; Interchange §Zotero Snapshot Input]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. Vocabulary pins and registry-upgrade consequences are documented, but the migration layout is not: no Zotero, userdata, or BBT version is named anywhere; the 'certified schema fixture matrix' is undefined; the required `better-bibtex.sqlite` member is obsolete from BBT 8.0 (keys moved to native `citationKey`, pinning removed); no sidecar (`-journal`/`-wal`) rule exists. The target profile is pinned to BibLaTeX 3.22, which no consumer on the user's machine runs; the real consumers (Pandoc's reader, classic `bibtex` with a `.bst`, Biber 2.21) are not named. [F-I06, F-I10]
- [x] CHK031 Are parser suitability and target-format limitations described as evidence-dependent assumptions rather than guarantees inherited from package selection? [Assumption, Research §R3; Spec §SC-010]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied. Research R3 and Plan §Technical Context call `bibtexparser` provisional and state that neither selection nor parsing proves fidelity. Executed experiments show the caution was warranted. [F-D01, F-D02]
- [x] CHK032 Are the user's paper/sample selection and external-content usability checks identified as acceptance dependencies with clear scope and authorization boundaries? [Dependency, Spec §A-08, §SC-001, §SC-002; Plan §Delivery Sequence and Validation Coverage]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied. A-08, SC-001/SC-002 and Plan §Release gates identify paper and sample selection and external-content checks as user-authorized acceptance dependencies. [no finding]

## Ambiguities and Conflicts

- [ ] CHK033 Is the distinction between required broad catalog usability and narrower initial output coverage explicit wherever the documents use “supported”? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-047, §FR-048; Bibliography §Independent coverage guarantees]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. 'Supported' is used for at least six different things without qualification (catalog type, value syntax, crossref pair, string reference, transliteration, schema layout), and FR-047's broad usability promise sits beside an export table that covers a fraction of admitted types. [F-Q03, F-I01]
- [x] CHK034 Are the container-and-part exception, minimum record identity, explicit-key requirements, and missing-title rules consistent across the spec and record contract? [Conflict, Spec §FR-001, §FR-003, §FR-006; Records §Source Creation; Bibliography B15]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied for consistency: FR-001, FR-003, FR-006, Records §Source Creation, Data model invariant 1 and B15 agree on the container-and-part exception and the explicit-key consequence. The B15 heuristic itself (dialect decides what `title` means) is unsafe for real files. [F-I04]
- [x] CHK035 Are deferred public citation formats, note/annotation editing, relationship management, and unrestricted custom bibliography processing consistently excluded? [Consistency, Spec §A-12; Bibliography §Named output profiles; Bibliographic model §Boundaries and compatibility claims]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Satisfied for consistency: A-12, Bibliography §Named output profiles, Bibliographic model §Boundaries and the CLI contract all exclude public CSL I/O, note/annotation editing and relationship management. The report disputes the CSL exclusion on its merits. [F-S03]
- [ ] CHK036 Is the authority of the new standards decision clear relative to recovered discussion, prior proposals, accepted conventions, and the revised feature requirements? [Traceability, Assumption, Spec §A-12; Bibliographic model §Intent and recovered context; Constitution §Governance]
  - Assessment (2026-09-20, evaluated): Not satisfied. `docs/bibliographic-model.md` is candid that the decision is a recommendation, but the spec states it as MUST-level scope and FR-047-FR-049 without a proposal marker, and cites the recovered discussion as evidence of intended breadth. The native transcript shows the user approved a process in which the assistant had said the Zotero baseline would be 'a proposal to evaluate, not ... an already accepted decision'. [F-S01, F-S04]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after reviewer evaluation of the written requirements. An agent may assist with that evaluation when explicitly asked.
- Leave unresolved or unevaluated items unchecked; record findings and needed clarification beside the relevant item. A `[Gap]`, `[Ambiguity]`, or `[Conflict]` marker identifies a review question, not a concluded defect.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist state as a gate and must not modify these markers.
- [requirements.md](requirements.md) has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- This invocation creates the checklist only. It does not evaluate items, revise requirements, or establish passing implementation evidence. No task list exists at generation time.

## Evaluation Record

- Evaluated on 2026-09-20 at the user's explicit request as part of the independent pre-task audit. All 36 items were evaluated; none is unevaluated. 16 are satisfied (`[x]`) and 20 are evaluated but not satisfied (`[ ]`). Item IDs, question text, and prior content are unchanged; each item gained one assessment sub-bullet.
- `[x]` here means the written requirements meet that requirements-quality criterion. It does not mean the underlying design choice is endorsed, implemented, or tested; several satisfied items carry findings about the substance of what is consistently specified.
- Finding IDs refer to the [audit report](../reviews/2026-09-20-independent-design-audit.md), which also lists checklist questions that are themselves flawed or miss an issue.
- The built-in [requirements.md](requirements.md) markers were reviewed and deliberately left unchanged; see finding F-Q01.
